{{Quote|Mandalore the Binder was born the son of a rug weaver on Harswee.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
A '''rug weaver''' was the [[Parent/Legends|parent]] of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Mandalore the Binder]], who was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on [[Harswee]],<ref name="TBHC" /> a world known for its luxurious loom-woven [[Carpet/Legends|carpet]] exports.<ref name="TCWIV">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> At some point between [[7000 BBY]] and [[60 BBY|60 BBY]],<ref name="Date">Per ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', Mandalore the Binder ruled as [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] after [[Mandalore the First/Legends|Mandalore the First]], whose reign ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates to approximately [[7000 BBY]]. ''The Bounty Hunter Code'' also establishes that ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', which mentions Mandalore the Binder's past reign, was supposedly [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;an authorship the authenticity of which was doubted by [[Jango Fett]]&mdash;at some point after the [[Battle of Galidraan]], which occurred in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]] per ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. Fett [[Showdown on Corellia|killed]] Vizsla during the main flashbacks of [[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 4]], the events of which ''[[The Cestus Deception]]'' dates to no less than three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the Battle of Galidraan and therefore no earlier than approximately [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]]. In addition, according to [[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 2]], Fett also held the title of Mandalore from the time of the [[Battle of Korda Six|death]] of the previous Mandalore, [[Jaster Mereel]], up until&mdash;per ''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''&mdash;his own [[Death/Legends|death]], which took place in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Per ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', Mereel became Mandalore in [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]], and ''Open Seasons'' 2 dates his death to thirty years before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] and thereby around [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]] per ''The New Essential Chronology''. Therefore, Mandalore the Binder must have ruled as Mandalore at some point between approximately 7000 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]] and 60 BBY.</ref> their son rose to become the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="TBHC" /> the traditional ruler of the Mandalorian clans.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> Mandalore the Binder was remembered alongside the rug weaver in ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', a manifesto supposedly written by [[Tor Vizsla]], the leader of the Mandalorian splinter group known as [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]&mdash;although the group's opponent [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] questioned the authenticity of Vizsla's authorship.<ref name="TBHC" /> At some point between [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="TBHCCreation">Per ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]'' was created after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] but before the [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] 39:3:22, which corresponds to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]]. {{Film|IV}} depicts Greedo's death during events ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].</ref> Jango's [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] son [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] included the manifesto in the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]''.<ref name="TBHC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The rug weaver was mentioned in the [[2013]] reference book ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''.<ref name="TBHC" />
